SevenUI primitives style themselves with the standard shadcn CSS variables (--background, --primary, --radius, …). If your project already has a shadcn theme, primitives adapt to it with no extra setup. Starting fresh? Install the default neutral tokens: Bash Package manager:npmpnpmyarnbun npx shadcn@latest add @sevenui/themepnpm dlx shadcn@latest add @sevenui/themeyarn dlx shadcn@latest add @sevenui/themebunx --bun shadcn@latest add @sevenui/theme Dark mode works through your existing .dark class strategy — the variables carry both palettes. One thing the token install can’t do for you: Tailwind v4’s dark: variant follows the operating system by default, so on a hand-rolled setup the primitives’ dark: utilities ignore your .dark class. npx shadcn init writes the opt-in for you; if you wired Tailwind up yourself, add it to the same stylesheet: CSS @custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *)); Status colors Alongside --destructive, the theme defines two more semantic pairs for status surfaces: --success / --success-foreground and --warning / --warning-foreground. Use them the way you use destructive (text-success, bg-warning/10) instead of reaching for a raw Tailwind green or amber, so status stays on-palette in both modes. They are fixed constants — unlike the base and accent colors, they don’t shift when you change the rest of the theme. Was this page helpful? Yes No Thanks for your feedback!
